Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle. Tim Seifert and Finn Allen are the two openers for New Zealand. Shaheen Afridi to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
…THE RUN CHASE…

Right then, New Zealand needs 136 runs to go 2-0 up in the series. Can they do it or will Pakistan show some fight and come back hard with the ball? We shall find out. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Ish Sodhi is up for a chat. He says that this ground is usually a spinner's graveyard, and this is a great batting wicket. Adds that Pakistan have put up a good score but they should be able to chase it down. Mentions that you need to protect the straighter boundary and picking up wickets at regular intervals helped them. Says that Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf can be threats, and they need to be wary of them despite them playing a spinner less.

New Zealand were tidy with the ball and on the field. They took their catches and never allowed Pakistan to get away with the game. It was a combined effort from all the bowlers where Jacob Duffy, Ben Sears, James Neesham, and Ish Sodhi, all chipped in with a couple of wickets each and kept the visitors to a below par score.

A slightly improved batting effort from Pakistan gets them to a decent score of 135/9 from their 15 overs. Having been sent into bat first, Pakistan struggled early on and lost their openers early but Salman Agha played an impressive knock of 46 off 28 balls and kept the innings together. Wickets kept falling at regular intervals and Salman Agha too fell in the 10th over. Handy cameos from Shadab Khan and Shaheen Afridi took the score past the 130-run mark.

OUT! RUN OUT! James Neesham bowls another wide yorker, on off, Shaheen Afridi jams it out towards sweeper covers and turns around for the second. Michael Bracewell is quick to pick up the ball and throw it at the bowler's end on the bounce. James Neesham collects it and breaks the stumps with Rauf well short of his crease. Pakistan finishes on 135/9!

Commentary.Commentary: We are done with the pre-match formalities. The players are making their way out to the middle. Mohammad Haris and Hasan Nawaz will open the batting for Pakistan. It will be Jacob Duffy with the ball in hand for New Zealand. Let's play...
The teams and match officials make their way to the ground for the National Anthems. We start with the anthem of Pakistan, followed by that of New Zealand. Live action is coming shortly.

Pitch Report - Grant Elliott and Frankie MacKay are at the pitchside. They share that the pitch has a nice covering of grass and will do a bit for the seamers. They add that there will be some sideways movement and a bit of bounce and that will skid on nicely. They mention that it will be a challenge for the spinners with short boundaries on either side.

Salman Agha, the skipper of Pakistan says that they are aware of putting in a good effort today. States that when you come to New Zealand, there will be extra bounce and they are ready for it. Adds that they have a talented squad and they are looking forward to this game. Ends by sharing that Haris Rauf comes in for Abrar Ahmed.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the second T20I in the five-match series between New Zealand and Pakistan, from the University Oval in Dunedin. In the opening match, Pakistan suffered a heavy defeat by 9 wickets, with nearly 10 overs to spare, and will be keen to come out with a much better effort today.
...MATCH DAY...

The T20I series between New Zealand and Pakistan shifts to Dunedin, where the University Oval will host the second match of the five-game contest. The hosts dominated the opening encounter with a commanding victory and will look to build on that momentum. Meanwhile, Pakistan, aiming for a fresh start in the format, had a forgettable outing, getting bowled out for just 91. Their batting inexperience showed as they went too hard too soon, failing to read the conditions and adapt. Four of their top six batters fell for single-digit scores, resulting in Pakistan’s fifth-lowest total in T20I history. With a relatively new-look batting lineup, the onus will be on skipper Salman Agha, Shadab Khan, and Mohammad Haris to step up. New Zealand, on the other hand, were nearly flawless in the first T20I. The only blemish was a couple of dropped chances in the field, something they will look to improve. Kyle Jamieson made a dream return to the T20I setup, picking up three wickets, while the rest of the bowling unit chipped in effectively. Interestingly, the last T20I played at the University Oval was also between these two teams and turned out to be a high-scoring affair. With both Men's Super Smash games earlier this year at this venue also producing plenty of runs this season, expect another entertaining contest. Will Pakistan regroup and mount a strong comeback? Or will New Zealand tighten their grip on the series and extend their lead? We shall find out.
